text:
Dario: Heads-up 10am sync tomorrow. Need a slim battlecard for the webinar audience (platform architects + infra buyers). Goal: 3 quick counters, 1 sticky metaphor, routing suggestions for inbound form.
Priya: Nice. Can we center on operational guarantees rather than raw model catalog? They already see models everywhere.
Dario: Exactly 1 prefer: 1) SLA-first serving (latency/availability guarantees), 2) predictable unit economics (reserved + batching), 3) deployment parity (hosted -> private VPC -> on-prem).
Omar: I've got new throughput numbers on long sequences: at seq=2048 our dedicated pool sustains 18 tps steady-state vs CloudY's bursty 9 tps on similar hardware (internal perf harness). Want that cited?
Jen: Yes but make it friendly: "sustained throughput at long contexts" is the callout. Avoid model-name bashing.
Nia: For the sticky metaphor: "Think of the model as the engine; Redwood is the road and traffic rules." Short, visual.
Priya: Love the metaphor. For inbound routing, recommend two buckets: 1) SMB/demo leads -> self-serve resources + API quickstart, 2) Enterprise -> AE handoff with reserved capacity checklist + security questionnaire.
Dario: Good. Also we need two rebut lines vs infra vendors that emphasize the developer DX: "Same API across all deployment modes" and "no forklift rework for go-live".
Omar: Adding a small ops note: can highlight canary policy: 5% traffic for 2 hours, monitor latency and error-rate deltas <10% before rollout.
deploy-bot: Canary policy template copied to marketing assets: `/infra/policies/canary-template.md`.
Jen: Also add a short callout on quality guardrails: prompt-sets + evals tied to rollouts, with automatic regression alerts. Makes the case we operationalize evaluation.
Nia: On the unit economics claim, use phrasing "reduces per-token spend through continuous batching and prefix-KV caching" and link to the cost explainer page. Don't state a blanket percent without a linked study.
Priya: I'll assemble a one-pager draft with a header, 3 bullets, 2 micro-case snippets (SaaS checkout latency win; legal corp on-prem compliance) and the inbound routing play.
Dario: Timeline: draft by 5pm today, review in the sync, finalize before speaker rehearsal. Jen, Nia, Omar 1 please review the draft for tech accuracy.
Jen: I'm in after 3pm.
Omar: Will drop perf summary and the test harness link: https://perf.redwood/longseq-2026
Nia: I'll write the metaphor and the enterprise routing paragraph.
Priya: Draft will be here: https://git.redwood/marketing/assets/webinar-battlecard-ops.json
Dario: Perfect. Quick ask: include two small footnotes: one linking to the cost model, one linking to the rollout policy. Keep the surface area <1 page. Thanks everyone!
